speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: When is an oligopoly market structure harmful to consumers?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: And how do we help consumers find the best fuel prices, regardless of crude oil price or market structure?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Brent Crude is the most commonly used benchmark in the world.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The United States generally relies on a different benchmark, the West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Crude, which fell from US$18 to minus US$38 per barrel on 20 April.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Observers have cited the much reduced demand for oil because of the COVID-19 situation as a key factor in explaining the trends for both cases.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: At the same time, supply has far exceeded demand.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: So, inventory was filling up, and in a number of markets there was lack of storage space.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Some analysts have noted that WTI Crude oil faced an acute shortage of storage space and thus traders were paying money in order to offload expiring contracts that carry a commitment to receive WTI Crude this month; hence, the negative trading prices for WTI Crude.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: What does this mean for Singapore and Singaporeans?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: While a drop in oil prices generally results in a drop in retail petrol price, this may not always happen, because of many other factors which affect retail petrol price.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: I seek your indulgence as I explain why.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The refining process separates the hydrocarbons in crude oil into different products such as retail petrol, jet fuels, bunker fuels, asphalt and naphtha.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: So, if there is a change in demand for one of the refined products, it can affect the supply and demand situation for the others.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The demand for jet fuel has dramatically fallen because of travel restrictions around the world.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Hence, refineries will need to store the excess jet fuel supply, reduce the price of jet fuel to move the supply, or reduce the production of jet fuel altogether.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Storing excess supply is only viable and sustainable if the refinery has enough storage space, with the assumption that this excess supply could eventually be sold.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Reducing the price of jet fuel may not move the supply much, if jet planes are not flying – as we have seen with the fall in demand due to travel restrictions from COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: And if the demand for jet fuel continues to be low, the refinery may decide to reduce the production of jet fuel by refining less crude oil.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This will reduce the production of other refined products, including retail petrol.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: And this would exert upward pressure on their prices despite no change to the underlying demand.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This effect could be more pronounced and persist in the medium to longer term if more refineries across the world shut down temporarily or for good, due to a mixture of the impact of COVID-19 and persistent low demand.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Another potential outcome of low demand and full inventory is that refineries will likely need more time to sell their products before they can bring in a new supply of crude.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: If the refineries are still processing crude oil purchased before the plunge in prices, there may be a longer lag time before lower crude oil input prices can pass through to end products.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Hence, it is not certain that every plunge in crude oil prices would necessarily lead to a decrease in refined petrol cost.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Furthermore, in addition to the refined petrol cost, the price that consumers pay for petrol also depends on the petrol companies' operating costs, land costs, duties and taxes, and discounts and rebates.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Oligopoly is a market structure where there are only a few providers in the market.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Partly due to Singapore's relatively small market, an oligopolistic-type structure can be found in several sectors, including supermarkets and cinemas.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Harm can arise if there is anti-competitive behaviour among the firms, for example, collusion to mark-up prices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Furthermore, there was no observable pricing pattern, such as a clear price leader, either for price increases or price decreases.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Thirdly, how do we help consumers find the best fuel prices, regardless of crude oil price or market structure?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: I had previously mentioned that well-informed consumers are a key deterrent against unreasonable pricing decisions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: I highlighted the Consumers Association of Singapore (CASE)'s work on Fuel Kaki.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The Fuel Kaki Price Estimator empowers individual consumers to compare not just the retail pump prices, but also the effective price of petrol across retailers, based on the various discounts and rebates specifically applicable to them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Fuel Kaki also allows individual consumers to explore what effective price would be paid, if they used different combinations of discounts and rebates across different retailers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This customised information is more meaningful to consumers than providing fuel prices based on the best discounts, which the retailers may not apply to every individual.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I think the consumers are frustrated, because everytime there is a drop in crude prices, there seems to be a lack in the fall in pump prices.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Whereas, the minute there is increase in crude oil prices, pump prices rise quite quickly.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: While the CASE is happy to work with CCCS to provide fuel prices in Fuel Kaki, I am just wondering whether MTI would be able to ask the fuel companies, in the interest of price transparency, to consider asking the fuel companies to provide or publish a breakdown of their costs components.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: That means the base costs of crude oil, the taxes, the land costs, their labour costs and so on.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: This will be similar to what One Motoring or LTA publishes insofar as the price of cars are concerned.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: One Motoring publishes the Open Market Value (OMV), the Additional Registration Fee (ARF), the taxes as well as the base costs of cars.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: For consumers, I think it will help if they are able to understand what are the crude oil prices, what is the fuel component of it, so that when a fuel companies increase their prices, then they would know how much more the fuel companies are charging for the the fuel component of the costs.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: If I can address his first point, which is whether petrol companies pass through more of the price change and at a faster rate when the crude oil prices go up, as compared to a decrease.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: And the answer is that, if you look at the empirical evidence, it does not suggest listed retail petrol prices adjust downwards more slowly or by a smaller amounts compared to upward price adjustments.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: This finding applied to both increases and decreases in price.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: The Member also asked about the components of listed petrol prices.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Some of the information that the Member is interested in may well be commercially sensitive, but we are prepared to work with CASE, with our agencies and with the companies to see whether there are ways to put more of this information out there.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: First, I want to thank Speaker for the opportunity to ask the questions and I also thank the Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the comprehensive reply.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: The fact that we have many questions over the last few months about fuel price, means that a lot of Members of the Parliament and also members of the public are not convinced that oil companies are behaving fairly.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: The fact that the five oil companies are making a lot of money, also adds to the suspicions.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: I like what Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat said about the food delivery companies at the last sitting.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Senior Minister of State Chee said that it may not be wise to cap the commission fees of the food delivery companies and the better way is to inject competition.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Thus, MTI is encouraging the restaurants and food outlets to engage the delivery companies under the Food Delivery Booster Package.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: In that way, the end customers can get food from the food outlets directly without going through the food delivery companies.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: So, in the same way, I would ask a supplementary question.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Will MTI consider injecting competition to the local petroleum market?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: And there are two options, one is to remove the three-quarter tank rule, so that Singapore motorists can go to Johor Bahru to pump petrol when COVID-19 is over.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: However, Singapore Government will lose the petrol tax if the Singapore cars go over to Johor Bahru to buy petrol.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: The second option is to allow white pump operators to sell fuel to the general public instead of selling the fuel to their own the fleet of vehicles only.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: This is similar to the practice amongst the telcos where some of the players are buying bulk from the existing telcos, repackage these and sell broadband connection at a lower price to the end customers.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: So, I hope MTI can consider injecting competition into the local petrol market to silence the criticism that major oil companies are profiteering.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: If I take a bit of time, please cheer me on with "加油".

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: On the question about the three-quarter tank rule, the three-quarter tank rule is part of a suite of policy measures to encourage less car usage and reduce carbon emissions.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: The Government will continue to ensure a well-functioning competitive petrol market against this backdrop.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: There was also a question that the Member raised, about what some have called "white pump fuel dispensing".

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: The idea, essentially, is, if you have a company that maintains a stock of fuel on site – some of these companies may do so because of a vehicle fleet – whether this stock can be sold onwards to consumers.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We are prepared to look at his suggestion and to consider it.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: But any consideration has to be done very carefully because there would have to be factors such as implications for land use and land allocation as well as ensuring safety for this.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: The other issue that the Member alludes to is: how do we improve transparency in a way that the consumer, on a day-to-day basis, has that information easily.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We can very much understand the interest in the listed pump prices.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: That, to date, has formed a lot of the discussion and discourse among members of the public.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: When you talk to uncles and aunties, it is often the listed pump prices that are at the top of the mind.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: But the listed prices can be different from the effective prices, which are what individual consumers pay after discounts and rebates.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: This prevented consumers from having the necessary information readily available to make the best petrol purchase decision.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: The Fuel Kaki website does not just collate the listed pump prices.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: That is what you see at the top of the handout.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: So, if you look at the handouts, what you can see is that the retailer with the lowest listed price may not be the one with the lowest effective price.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: You would also see that although listed prices are the same for most retailers, effective prices do differ even without any promotions or discounts other than the loyalty programme.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: So, although the handout has quite a small font size, I thought I would bring your attention to Figure 2, which is the effective price that one can get based on the loyalty programme only.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: You can see the bars are not quite exactly the same length and not exactly the same value, and that is reflected in the handouts which we have distributed to Members.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Consumers can also tick multiple boxes on the Fuel Kaki website to search across multiple petrol retailers and across multiple discounts and rebate programmes to find the lowest effective price.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: So, if you are curious, you want to see what the other promotions, options, discounts and rebates are, you can search.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: I know of users who will tick all the boxes and then they click search and the website gives a whole list, much like what you see in Figures 3 and 4 of the handouts that you have.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: And this helps individual consumers also find out if a different retailer with different discounts and rebates can give a better lower effective price.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: And Fuel Kaki puts that into the palm of your hand, on your smartphone, and you can search within a minute.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: That information can help you in so many ways.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: If you are a consumer, you can search for the lowest effective price; if you are an academic, it helps to have a single portal which you can look up, and I am sure there are many learned economists in this House and outside who would be interested.
